text:
pagerduty (bot): PAGER — Canary failures detected for release r-2026-03-17 (us-west-2 canary pool). Error rate spike 12% -> 45% on predict endpoints. Pager: P2.
ashley (SRE): acked, paging oncall. tagging @jia.
jia (oncall): oncall here, pulling logs and health dashboards now. opening a short incident channel.
sam.k (release lead): pausing rollout in all regions. can we stop the traffic shift? :eyes:
ashley (SRE): issuing rollout freeze and disabling gradual ramp in routing. sending kill-switch for feature flag to stop traffic to canary instances.
deploy-bot: rollout: r-2026-03-17 status -> PAUSED by ashley. feature-flag: r2026_release -> toggled OFF for canary.
matt (prod eng): quick check — are these failures latency spikes or 5xx?
jia (oncall): mostly 5xx (503/502) during generation heavy paths. CPU/GPU metrics show increased queuing on canary hosts.
ashley (SRE): hypothesis: new model variant has a compatibility regression under short sequences -> KV cache growth.
sam.k (release lead): we need rollback plan. prefer automated fallback to previous model if safe, else manual rollback of canary nodes.
matt (prod eng): I can trigger automated model-fallback if runtime health check supports it. preparing command.
jia (oncall): while matt readies fallback, let's prepare manual rollback in case automation fails. support-ops please prepare customer comms draft.
support-ops: noted. drafting: "We're investigating intermittent errors on generation endpoints affecting a subset of customers in us-west-2. We'll update in 30 minutes"
ashley (SRE): manual rollback commands (for oncall) — revert canary VM group to image r-2026-03-16 and drain traffic: ```
# drain traffic from canary pool
redwoodctl traffic drain --pool canary-usw2 --timeout 300
# revert model version on serving group
redwoodctl serving set-model --group canary-usw2 --model redwood-v1.8.2
# smoke test
curl -s -X POST https://canary-proxy.usw2.internal/generate -d '{"prompt":"smoke"}' | jq
```
jia (oncall): executing drain now. running revert after drain completes.
deploy-bot: drain started for pool canary-usw2 (nodes: 6). expected drain window 5m.
ashley (SRE): while draining, enable prefix KV cache clear on canary pool to avoid stale state if we flip models: ```
redwoodctl cache flush --pool canary-usw2 --prefix kv/
```
jia (oncall): drain completed. starting model revert.
matt (prod eng): model revert started. watching.
ashley (SRE): verifying smoke tests and latency SLOs for reverted nodes.
jia (oncall): smoke test responses OK on 5/6 nodes, one node still returning 502, taking it out of rotation.
matt (prod eng): removed bad node and rebalanced. overall 5xx down to 2%.
sam.k (release lead): good. holding rollback stable for 15m then slowly resume canary with guardrails.
support-ops: customer update queued: "Rollback to previous model completed. Errors reduced significantly; we're monitoring. We'll post ETA for full resume in 30m"
ashley (SRE): monitoring logs and error budget. pushing an immediate postmortem stub to #postmortems. please add timelines and any config commits.
jia (oncall): incident closed to P2 -> mitigated, will remain on watch for 45m. final note — automation fallback failed to trigger due to missing health-check label; opening ticket to add test coverage.
sam.k (release lead): noted. we'll add health-check label before next rollout. thanks all :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: rollout: r-2026-03-17 status -> ROLLBACK_COMPLETE (canary).
ashley (SRE): end notes: customers affected: subset of hosted customers in us-west-2 (~0.6% of total traffic). no data loss. next steps: postmortem, add automated health-check label, and update rollout playbook.
support-ops: publishing status update to customers now."
